newsitem.title: UK: Mark crosses feeble as dollar/mark regains energy.
newsitem.headline: Mark crosses feeble as dollar/mark regains energy.

text.p: The mark languished against its European counterparts as mark sentiment was dominated by the dollar's renewed bout of energy against the German currency.
With no new factors emerging to affect the European currencies, the mark crosses were simply tracking dollar/mark for now, traders said.

"Everyone's watching to see if dollar/mark has the strength to go above 1.85 and at the U.S. payrolls figures (due later today) and dollar/yen's strength. There's nothing new in the EMS currencies themselves today," said one trader at a U.S. bank in London.
The dollar had been given a leg-up overnight by U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin, who reiterated that a strong dollar was in the U.S. interest.
Dollar/mark had risen towards the seven-and-a-half year high of 1.8490 it had set Monday, and the mark had edged lower on the crosses in line with the move.
The mark was at 3.3708/13 French francs at 0930 GMT against its late Thursday European level of 3.3721/23. Mark/lira was at 975.35/55 against 975.70/60.

New developments in European monetary union were unlikely to emerge for now with political activity slowing down in Europe for the summer, so the mark crosses will probably stick to range-trading until the Bundesbank sets the conditions for its next securities repurchase tender on August 12.

Speculation regarding the Bundesbank's repurchase tenders has been swirling in the market since the central bank, at its council meeting last Thursday, fixed the repo rate for only the first two weeks of its four-week summer break.
The Bundesbank made clear its decision was aimed at keeping open its options on rate policy, and that it was considering conducting floating and fixed rate repos at the same time.

"Because of all the interest in the Bundesbank's decision to leave open the question of whether the repo rate will go higher or not, people squared a lot of their short mark positions this week," said Ernesto Ramirez, European economist at Bankers Trust.

"But maybe we're already seeing a retracement of the mark after that (rise)... And people are thinking that although it (switching to floating repos) would be a good move, how much is it going to change the big picture for the mark?" Ramirez said.
Meanwhile, the mark was also tracking the dollar's slip against the Swiss franc this morning. Mark/Swiss was at its session lows of 82.02/04 centimes against its late Thursday level of 82.35/40.

The Irish punt was shedding the gains it made against the mark earlier when it was recovering from its slide on Thursday, when punt/mark weakened in line with the Irish currency's drop against sterling.
The punt was at its session low of 2.6780/20, down from the high of 2.6896 but still above late Thursday's 2.6700/50.
